findings.pdf_says: 6.3.1.1.1 Comparison of Numeric Operands ... 6.3.1.1.2 Comparison of Nonnumeric Operands
findings.markdown_says: ### 6.3.1.1.1 Comparison of Numeric Operands ... ### 6.3.1.1.2 Comparison of Nonnumeric Operands
findings.why_it_matters: These are subclauses of 6.3.1.1 Relation Condition, which the transcription heads at level 4 (`#### 6.3.1.1 Relation Condition`), yet they are headed at level 3 (`###`), the same level as `### 6.3.1 Simple Conditions`. The heading tree makes them siblings of 6.3.1 rather than children of 6.3.1.1, so any tool that slices the document by heading hierarchy detaches them from the Relation Condition clause.

findings.markdown_says: ### 6.3.1.1.3 Comparisons Involving Index-Names and/or Index Data Items ... ### 6.3.1.2 Class Condition
findings.why_it_matters: 6.3.1.1.3 is a child of `#### 6.3.1.1 Relation Condition` but is headed at level 3, and 6.3.1.2 Class Condition is a sibling of 6.3.1.1 (level 4) and of 6.3.1.3/6.3.1.4/6.3.1.5 (all `####` on page 290) but is headed `###`, the level of its parent `### 6.3.1 Simple Conditions`. The heading hierarchy no longer matches the clause numbering.

findings.pdf_says: The box enclosing 6.3.1.3 Condition-Name Condition (Conditional Variable) runs unbroken from the heading through the general format line "condition-name-1" to the final paragraph; the general format sits inside the box.
findings.why_it_matters: Every other line of 6.3.1.3 carries the ║ box marker, and the boxed general formats on pages 290-293 (sign condition, NOT condition-1, combined and abbreviated combined conditions) carry ║/╔╚ markers inside the pre block, but the condition-name condition's general format does not. The box marks the content as belonging to the boxed (higher-level) material, so this general format reads as unboxed, unlike the printed page.
